yt.title: Why {f_a} + {f_b} is not {f_target} in code #Shorts
yt.description:
Computed live in Python with IEEE 754 double precision floats: {f_a} + {f_b} = {f_sum}. Equal to {f_target}: {f_equal}.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.narration: In most programming languages, zero point one plus zero point two is not zero point three.

scenes.label: what the computer actually returns
scenes.narration: The computer returns zero point three, followed by a long tail of zeros and a four. We computed this just now.
Computers store numbers in binary. Zero point one has no exact binary form, just like one third has no exact decimal form.
So never compare floats with equals. Check that the difference is tiny instead. For money, use integers.
